lead_profile_text: Existing property looking for higher return
stl_goal: Reduce management costs before his current fee rises from 20% to 24% at renewal (~Sep/Oct 2026), while preserving his established 80-review Airbnb listing
property_situation: EX-STL — live on Airbnb since 2020, currently managed by another company for ~4 years; 80 reviews, 4.84 rating; ~80% booked since March, back-to-back in August; Nov–Jan historically quiet (current company secures 4-month winter long-lets); review gap Oct 2024–Sep 2025; priced ~20% above comparable Lincoln listings; also owns a second Airbnb property (outbuilding) in London
property_type: 2-bed / 3-bath leasehold apartment, gated cul-de-sac development, city centre
primary_blocker: Needs 2-3 weeks to confirm his renewing mortgage rate, check whether October remains empty on the booking calendar, and speak to his current management company before committing to switch

get back to you in like a few days

delay_signals.context: Needs to confirm his renewing mortgage rate and check whether October stays empty on the booking calendar (the intended migration window) before committing to switch.

delay_signals.trigger_phrase: I'll have a speak with them and this is this whole thing is going to come as part of a big conversation anyway

green_light_signals.trigger_phrase: Mortgage is I think September October this year
green_light_signals.context: Current management fee increase (20%→24%) and mortgage rate renewal both land in the same Sep/Oct 2026 window, creating a concrete forcing deadline that aligns with wanting to switch soon; October/November also happens to be his quietest season, making it a natural migration window.

green_light_signals.trigger_phrase: I'm sure they wouldn't mind that. I mean I have all the logins and I can just change the email addresses
green_light_signals.context: Gregory has full access/control of his existing listing, no operational complaints against his current provider, and is willing to hand over credentials to migrate once he decides.

But I mean, I could just go through some income estimations to start with so we can say what we can say we are estimating to achieve. zac_language.numbers_framing: Led with headline gross/net figures (£66k gross / £34k net, ~£2,800-2,900/month) before dwelling on fees, then reconciled the lead's own lower actual revenue against the projection with specific, concrete factors (review gap dates, ~20% price premium) rather than disputing his numbers
zac_language.objection_handling_pattern: Validates the lead's own data point first, then supplies a specific, evidence-based explanation (review gap, price premium) rather than defending the projection in the abstract; reframes potential negatives (review reset risk, migration downtime) as manageable and time-limited rather than dismissing the concern

what_they_focused_on: operational mechanics of the migration/deactivation process
how his own actual revenue compares to Zac's projection
what_they_needed_most: a concrete, credible explanation for why his own revenue is lower than the projection
reassurance that he wouldn't lose his review history by switching
clarity on exact migration mechanics and timing
profile_psychology_intersection.recommended_meeting_adjustment: For analytical EX-STL switchers driven by fee increases rather than service failures, lead with the listing-migration mechanics and review-preservation plan earlier — before the income projection — since protecting existing history is the primary anchor, and be ready to proactively reconcile projected figures against the lead's own actual performance data rather than waiting for pushback.
